style: Style references only: the attached images set the painting style, the colours and the mood. Do not copy their content. Paint it as a concept artist's painted sketch sheet for a cozy, bright strategy game: loose hand-painted brushwork with visible strokes, soft painted light from a warm sunny afternoon coming from the front right, cheerful bright colours, a warm light cream paper background with a soft painted shadow under each object. It is a painting, not a 3D render, not low poly, not a game screenshot. Cozy and friendly like a storybook toy, never grim. No people, no text, no labels, no numbers, no letters, no watermark.

frames.sheet:
{style}

The sheet shows the rampart of a toy fortress built from chunky full-tile blocks on a board of square tiles of bright green grass, seen in a three-quarter view from well above, the way a board game is seen from a chair. Every block fills one whole square tile and stands about three quarters as tall as the tile is wide, so the rampart is a thick square-section wall with a flat stone walkway along its top and a grid of two by two square merlons, the teeth of a battlement, standing on each block's walkway. The stone is warm cream with crisp edges and narrow flat bevels, and blocks that share a side join into one continuous wall. One straight run of four blocks turns a corner and continues for three more blocks; the two blocks at the far end carry a second storey of the same block stacked on top, twice as tall, with merlons only on the upper storey. Below the run, smaller and alone on its own grass tile, stands one single block seen a little closer so its sides show. {look}

directions.look: The look: every face of every block carries one blind arch, a round-headed recess like the arch of a medieval doorway with no door and no opening behind it, sunk a hand's width into the stone, its dark half-round shadow repeating along the run, with a plain pier of stone between neighbouring arches. The walkway and the merlons stay plain.

The look: the body of each block is set back a little on every side, so the wall is thinner in the middle and fatter at the top and at the foot. A low plinth as wide as the tile runs along the ground, and the walkway with its merlons overhangs the body on a row of small stone corbels, like a machicolated parapet, casting a deep shadow line under the overhang.

The look: a square pilaster strip stands proud at every block corner, from the ground up to a projecting string course band just under the walkway, so the run reads as a row of shallow buttresses with slightly recessed stone panels between them. The walkway and the merlons stay plain.

The look: the faces are built of big rectangular blocks of dressed stone in three courses with deep recessed joints, carved grooves and not drawn lines, each stone about as long as the tile is wide and the courses offset like brickwork. The walkway and the merlons stay plain.

The look: the body is a plain smooth slab, but a cornice band projects a little from every face just under the walkway, and every merlon wears a low four-sided pyramid cap, like the roof of a tiny tower, so the tops of the wall sparkle with small lit facets.

The look: two separate ramparts stand side by side on the same board with a wide gap of grass between them. The left rampart has a set-back body with the walkway and merlons overhanging on small corbels, and its walkway and the tops of its merlons are stained royal blue. The right rampart has pilaster strips at every block corner under a string course, and its walkway and merlon tops are stained deep purple. The stone of both stays warm cream, and the ground enclosed by each rampart is stamped tan mud with a faint wash of that rampart's colour.
